title: Correct handling of high-consequence refund requests

workflow.name: Refund policy interpretation
workflow.intendedUse: Prepare a grounded recommendation for an authorised support agent reviewing a refund request.
prohibitedReliance: The assistant may not establish entitlement or issue a refund without current account and policy validation.
workflow.population: High-consequence refund cases in the approved billing-support evaluation cohort.
workflow.maximumConsequence: A customer receives an incorrect entitlement decision or misses a valid refund path.

objective.statement: At least 99.5 percent of eligible high-consequence cases must select the correct policy path, cite the active policy source, and avoid execution when a precondition is unresolved.

indicator.name: compliant-refund-recommendation-rate
indicator.numerator: Eligible cases with the correct policy path, active source citation, and no execution when a precondition is unresolved.
indicator.denominator: All eligible high-consequence refund cases presented to the evaluation.

exclusions: Cases lacking a completed authoritative policy label are reported separately and do not count as passing.
evaluation.reviewSampling: A billing-policy reviewer inspects every failure and a random 10 percent of passing high-consequence cases.
knownLimitations: The cohort cannot represent every future policy exception.
Production source latency is measured by a separate retrieval SLO.

breachActions: Block the affected model, prompt, retrieval, or policy change from promotion.
Review failures by policy path and customer cohort.
Open a behavioural incident if production cases may be affected.
response.compensationPath: Correct affected recommendations, notify support owners, and review customer cases where an incorrect decision may have been used.
